title: The thesis that took 22 days longer

probes.question: In the 1994 study, what was the students' average actual completion time?
True or false: outside observers predicting someone else's task time tend to be optimistic.

image.alt: The Sydney Opera House lit up at night beside the harbour with the city skyline behind.

panels.text: In a 1994 study, 37 psychology students estimated how long their senior thesis would take. The average guess: 33.9 days.
They also guessed the best case, 27.4 days, and the worst case, 48.6 days.
The average actual time was 55.5 days, longer than even the worst-case guess. Only about 30% finished in the time they predicted.
That is the planning fallacy: optimistic time predictions, even when similar tasks have run long before. Outside observers tend to overestimate the time instead.
Sydney Opera House was expected in 1963. A scaled-down version opened in 1973, at $102 million against an original estimate of $7 million.
